body.segment: This paper presents a phase-modulated high-frequency isolated dc/ac converter as the grid interface in a distributed generation system.
The converter includes two full-bridge HF LCL-type resonant inverters working at fixed duty cycle.
The power control is realized by means of the phase-shift between the two bridges.
Using the LCL-type resonant tank, zero-voltage-switching is achieved for all switches for the whole power range.
With the phase-shift modulated sinusoidally, a full-wave rectified output current synchronized with the utility line is obtained, which is unfolded and fed to the single-phase utility line.
The analysis is verified with computer simulation results.
Experimental data based on a 500-W prototype circuit is included for validation purpose.
